decision_reason: A1 provides useful posture, motion magnitude, periodicity, impact, rotation and translation concepts, but jumping remains close to descending stairs and running through shared high impulsiveness and motion intensity. The high D_kNN values for moving around in an elevator, standing in an elevator still and jumping also indicate that transfer would benefit from a supported distinction beyond the existing attributes. Add an impact-specific temporal structure attribute while preserving the physically interpretable A1 concepts.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: impact_periodicity
attributes.definition: Degree to which short-duration impact or loading events recur with a stable temporal structure.

levels.Low: No clear recurring impact or loading sequence.
levels.Medium: Recurring impact or loading events with moderate temporal consistency.
levels.High: Clearly recurring impact or loading events with a stable temporal structure.

operations.reason: Adds an independent temporal description of recurring impact or loading events, separating impact magnitude from impact timing. Supporting groups are G6, G10 and G11, with G3 providing corroborating motion-energy evidence; torso and leg IMUs can observe repeated loading peaks and their timing. The attribute is expected to transfer from descending stairs and running to jumping, where recurring impacts can be temporally structured even when cadence or overall regularity differs. semantic_redundancy_review: The retained attributes describe different observable dimensions: motion_intensity measures overall energy; cadence measures repetition rate; motion_regularity measures predictability; smoothness measures sustained continuity; impulsiveness measures peak abruptness; impact_periodicity measures the timing structure of impact events; posture_inclination measures mean gravity-relative configuration; posture_variability measures its change; rotational_motion measures angular activity; and translational_motion measures sustained locomotor progression. Smoothness, impulsiveness and impact_periodicity are related but remain separable through continuous fluctuation, peak magnitude and recurrence timing. Cadence and motion_regularity are also related but distinguish rate from temporal predictability. All final concepts are supported in principle by the listed G1-G14 capabilities and the torso, arm and leg accelerometer-gyroscope inventory.
